chip: La Chine contrôle le marché du pétrole
title: 17. Comment la Chine a calmé le prix du pétrole pendant la guerre en Iran
gist: During the Iran war, oil prices stayed surprisingly stable even with the Strait of Hormuz largely shut — mainly because China cut its crude oil imports by nearly half, absorbing the shock. This shows China's buying power now rivals OPEC's, and this time it helped consumers rather than hurting them. But it's uncomfortable that an authoritarian government has this much market control, and the balance could shift back toward OPEC as global oil supply tightens later this decade.

body.fr: Pendant la guerre en Iran, le {{détroit d'Hormuz|Strait of Hormuz}} est presque fermé.

bd.meaning: During the Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz is almost closed.
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: {{Pourtant|however}}, le prix du pétrole {{reste|stays}} plutôt stable.

bd.meaning: However, the price of oil stays rather stable.
bd.key: rester = “to remain/stay.” A common verb for describing something that keeps a quality.
No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: La Chine {{réduit|reduces}} ses importations de pétrole de presque la moitié.

bd.meaning: China reduces its oil imports by almost half.
bd.key: “ses” = his/her/its. French doesn't mark the owner's gender — only what's owned.

body.fr: Elle {{utilise|uses}} ses grandes réserves {{au lieu d'acheter|instead of buying}} plus.

bd.meaning: It uses its large reserves instead of buying more.
bd.key: au lieu de + plain verb = “instead of.” Another little word that pairs with a plain verb.

body.fr: Ainsi, le monde {{évite|avoids}} un {{choc pétrolier|oil shock}}.

bd.meaning: This way, the world avoids an oil shock.
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: Depuis longtemps, {{c'est l'OPEP qui contrôle|it's OPEC that controls}} le marché du pétrole.

bd.meaning: For a long time, it's OPEC that controls the oil market.
bd.key: c'est … qui = “it's … that.” A way to put emphasis on who does the action.

body.fr: L'OPEP garde les prix {{élevés|high}} {{en limitant|by limiting}} la production.

bd.meaning: OPEC keeps prices high by limiting production.

body.fr: Mais maintenant, la Chine a presque le même {{pouvoir|power}}.

bd.meaning: But now, China has almost the same power.
chunks: la Chine a presque le même pouvoir
China has almost the same power
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: Cette fois, ce grand pouvoir {{aide|helps}} les consommateurs.

bd.meaning: This time, this great power helps consumers.
bd.key: No new pattern here — just useful vocabulary for the story.

body.fr: Mais {{c'est inquiétant|it's worrying}} : un gouvernement {{autoritaire|authoritarian}} a autant de contrôle.

bd.meaning: But it's worrying: an authoritarian government has this much control.
bd.key: Reuses c'est to introduce a judgment before explaining it — a common way to structure an opinion in French.

body.fr: Plus tard, la situation {{va peut-être changer|might change}}.

bd.key: aller + plain verb + peut-être softens the near future into “might.”

body.fr: Le monde {{va manquer|is going to lack}} de nouveaux {{champs pétroliers|oil fields}}.

bd.meaning: The world is going to lack new oil fields.
chunks: the world is going to lack
bd.key: Reuses aller + plain verb for the near future.

body.fr: Alors, l'OPEP {{peut redevenir|can become again}} plus forte.

bd.meaning: So, OPEC can become strong again.
bd.key: Reuses pouvoir + plain verb: peut redevenir = “can become again.”

grammar.fr: C'est l'OPEP qui contrôle le marché
grammar.en: c'est … qui = “it's … that.” Puts the spotlight on who performs the action.

grammar.fr: L'OPEP garde les prix élevés en limitant la production
grammar.en: en + -ant = “by doing.” Explains the method behind an action.

grammar.fr: Elle utilise ses réserves au lieu d'acheter plus
grammar.en: au lieu de + plain verb = “instead of.” Another little word (like pour and sans) that keeps the following verb plain.

quiz.q: Pourquoi le prix du pétrole reste-t-il stable pendant la guerre en Iran ?
quiz.a: Parce que la Chine réduit beaucoup ses importations et utilise ses réserves. (Because China greatly reduces its imports and uses its reserves.)

flag: I dropped the OPEC economic-damage statistics and the UAE's exit from the cartel to keep the story short. I also simplified un gouvernement autoritaire ait autant de contrôle into a plainer colon construction to avoid the subjunctive (ait) that a native speaker would naturally use there — correct A1 French, but not quite how an adult native would phrase the thought.
